question: Does a stronger baseline than plain additivity shrink the gap (bias, share beyond 2 sd, AUC), or is the gap real?

design.assays: 48 assays with >= 500 pairs (813,014 pairs), the README's correlation subset
design.scale: every residual in units of plain additivity's own per-assay residual sd (residual_scale_sd); the 2-sd threshold is therefore the same for every model

metrics.r2_resid_var: 1 - var(r - r_hat)/var(r): share of the additivity residual's variance removed; constant shifts score 0
metrics.mse_skill: 1 - mean((r - r_hat)^2)/mean(r^2): share of additivity's squared error removed, bias included
metrics.auc_direction: epsceil.pairs.direction_auc of the corrected prediction vs observed, via summarise_table
metrics.frac_outside_2sd: share of pairs with |r - r_hat| > 2, via summarise_table
metrics.frac_outside_2sd_centred: the same after mean-centring within assay (add_centred_columns)
metrics.spearman_additive: summarise_table's Spearman of the (corrected) prediction vs observed; the key keeps summarise_table's name
metrics.aggregation: median over assays of per-assay values; null = mean over permutations per assay, then median

design.inner_split: KFold(5, shuffle, random_state=seed) over each assay's pairs; every pair is scored by parameters fitted without it. Needs measured doubles from the same protein, which plain additivity does not.
design.outer_split: GroupKFold(5) over assays (one group per assay): ridge lambda per model = argmax of the median inner-CV r2_resid_var over the TRAINING assays; the pooled offset = median bias over the TRAINING assays
design.pair_term: rank-k symmetric approximation (largest |eigenvalues|) of the position x position matrix of the position model's training residuals; cell means weighted n/(n+lambda), unobserved cells and diagonal completed by EM for weighted low-rank approximation
design.null: 10 permutations per assay: the identical pipeline, including the outer lambda selection, with residuals permuted among the training pairs of each inner fold; scored against the REAL held-out residuals. The mean survives permutation, so offsets survive their nulls by construction.

caveats: Every per-assay row is fitted on 4/5 of the scored protein's own measured doubles. A lab that has only singles has none of them, so these rows bound what a stronger baseline can do; they are not a singles-only predictor.

The inner split is random over pairs, so a held-out pair usually shares both positions (and often a single mutation) with training pairs. That is the most favourable split for position terms; holding out whole position pairs was not run.

Position terms can absorb a global nonlinearity (for example a floor or saturation of the assay), because single-effect size clusters by position. A monotone global-epistasis fit was not run, so the position R2 is not evidence of position-SPECIFIC epistasis.

r2_resid_var is out-of-fold R2 of the SIGNED residual. The README's position figure (0.140) is in-sample R2 of |residual| grouped by position pair; the two are different quantities and are not comparable.
The pooled offset is expressed in each scored assay's residual-sd units; turning it into raw units needs that assay's residual sd, which comes from its doubles.

models.uses: one constant from the OTHER assays (GroupKFold(5) by assay); no residual of the scored assay enters it, but it is applied in that assay's residual-sd units, which come from its doubles
fitted on 4/5 of the scored assay's own doubles (inner KFold(5))
fitted on 4/5 of the scored assay's own doubles (inner KFold(5)); ridge lambda chosen by GroupKFold(5) over the other assays

verdict.bias: plain additivity -0.938 sd; pooled offset from other assays -0.067; own-assay offset -0.000 (null -0.000); additive+position+pair_rank3 +0.000 (null -0.000)
verdict.beyond_2sd: plain 0.126 -> pooled offset 0.067 -> own offset 0.046 -> additive+position+pair_rank3 0.025 (its null 0.045); plain centred 0.046
verdict.spread: additive+position+pair_rank3 removes a median 0.381 of the residual variance (null -0.006); additive+position alone 0.333 (null -0.001)

gap_survives.bias: median bias -0.938 sd -> -0.000 with the assay's own offset, and -0.000 under that offset's permutation null; -0.067 with one offset learned on the other assays
gap_survives.beyond_2sd: 0.126 plain -> 0.067 pooled offset -> 0.046 own offset (plain centred 0.046) -> 0.025 additive+position+pair_rank3; the position model's null 0.046
gap_survives.spread: the strongest baseline (additive+position+pair_rank3) leaves 0.619 of the residual variance: R2 0.381 against its null -0.006, above the null in 48/48 assays
gap_survives.ranking: median AUC 0.884 -> 0.905 (null 0.884); per-assay median gain +0.0081, above additive in 34/48 assays
gap_survives.needs_doubles: fitted on 4/5 of the scored assay's own doubles (inner KFold(5)); ridge lambda chosen by GroupKFold(5) over the other assays
